verses.text: “Cry aloud, don’t spare. Lift up your voice like a trumpet. Declare to my people their disobedience, and to the house of Jacob their sins.

Yet they seek me daily, and delight to know my ways. As a nation that did righteousness, and didn’t forsake the ordinance of their God, they ask of me righteous judgments. They delight to draw near to God.
‘Why have we fasted,’ say they, ‘and you don’t see? Why have we afflicted our soul, and you don’t notice?’ “Behold, in the day of your fast you find pleasure, and oppress all your laborers.
Behold, you fast for strife and contention, and to strike with the fist of wickedness. You don’t fast today so as to make your voice to be heard on high.

Is this the fast that I have chosen? A day for a man to humble his soul? Is it to bow down his head like a reed, and to spread sackcloth and ashes under himself? Will you call this a fast, and an acceptable day to Yahweh?
“Isn’t this the fast that I have chosen: to release the bonds of wickedness, to undo the straps of the yoke, to let the oppressed go free, and that you break every yoke?

Isn’t it to distribute your bread to the hungry, and that you bring the poor who are cast out to your house? When you see the naked, that you cover him; and that you not hide yourself from your own flesh?
Then your light will break out as the morning, and your healing will appear quickly; then your righteousness shall go before you; and Yahweh’s glory will be your rear guard.
Then you will call, and Yahweh will answer; you will cry for help, and he will say, ‘Here I am.’ “If you take away from among you the yoke, finger pointing, and speaking wickedly;
and if you pour out your soul to the hungry, and satisfy the afflicted soul: then your light will rise in darkness, and your obscurity will be as the noonday;
and Yahweh will guide you continually, and satisfy your soul in dry places, and make your bones strong; and you shall be like a watered garden, and like a spring of water, whose waters don’t fail.
Those who shall be of you shall build the old waste places; you shall raise up the foundations of many generations; and you shall be called Repairer of the Breach, Restorer of Paths with Dwellings.

“If you turn away your foot from the Sabbath, from doing your pleasure on my holy day; and call the Sabbath a delight, and the holy of Yahweh honorable; and shall honor it, not doing your own ways, nor finding your own pleasure, nor speaking your own words:
then you shall delight yourself in Yahweh; and I will make you to ride on the high places of the earth; and I will feed you with the heritage of Jacob your father:” for Yahweh’s mouth has spoken it.

footnotes.content: The prophet is called to *cry aloud*—not gently whisper, but speak plainly the thing no one wants to hear. I've learned that sometimes love means holding up a mirror, even when it stings.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They *delight to know God's ways*—yet miss the point. This is the hard truth: we can know Scripture, attend worship, even *feel close to God*—and still be far from His heart if we've lost justice and mercy.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They complain that God ignores their fasts. But Isaiah cuts through: on their fast days they *oppress their laborers*. The text shows us plainly—ritual discipline without justice is hollow, a performance God turns away from.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Fasting for *strife and contention*—using discipline as cover for violence and power. The saddest fast is one we keep to feed our pride or sharpen our fists.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Bowing heads, spreading ashes—outward signs of repentance. But God asks: *will you call this a fast?* As if to say, you can dress it up all you like, but I know who you are on the inside.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Now the true fast appears: *release the bonds of wickedness, let the oppressed go free*. This is what God chooses—not our privation, but our mercy. Every chain we break, every yoke we undo, is prayer He hears.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Distribute bread, bring the poor inside, cover the naked. Notice He doesn't say *consider their plight* or *feel sorry*—He says *do it*. Faith shows itself in the breaking of bread and the sharing of shelter.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: When we turn toward justice, light *breaks out as the morning*. Healing appears quickly. This is the strange promise: righteousness is its own reward, and God Himself guards our way.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: *Here I am.* God's answer comes instantly when we cry out—but notice the condition first: we must put away the yoke and the pointing finger. No accusing voice can speak justice into being.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: *Pour out your soul to the hungry*—spend yourself lavishly on those who suffer. Then, remarkably, *your light will rise in darkness*. The one who feeds others finds themselves fed by something deeper than bread.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Yahweh will guide, satisfy, strengthen—the promises flow like a river. We become a *watered garden* whose waters never fail. This is what growing old in faith looks like: nourished, fruitful, never abandoned.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: *Repairer of the Breach*—what a calling. Those who live justly become healers of the broken places in their communities, builders of what was left in ruins by others' negligence.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Even our rest must be holy—we honor the Sabbath not by chasing our pleasures, but by sanctifying the day. This teaches us that all of life, even our leisure, belongs to God.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Readers today hear an echo: when we turn from self-seeking toward justice and rest in God, He promises to *make you to ride on the high places* and *feed you with the heritage of Jacob*. The covenant stands firm for those who truly seek Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
